description.value: This study examined gray and white matter volume differences between cocaine-dependent individuals and non-drug using controls and tested whether impulsivity dimensions were differentially associated with regional gray matter volume between groups.

spans.text: We used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses (VBM) to detect differences in gray matter (GM) and white matter (WM) volumes between cocaine users and controls, and to measure differences in the way that impulsivity relates to GM and WM volumes in cocaine users vs. controls.

description.value: This was a cross-sectional observational study of cocaine-dependent individuals and non-drug using controls, with assessments conducted across two sessions separated by less than one week and MRI scanning in the second session.
